title: Diagnostic: private Is Private
hints: `private` members are only visible inside the type (and its extensions in the same file).
Mark `secret` as `private` and keep the read from top-level code.
jsBridge: `private` restricts access to the enclosing declaration and its extensions in the same file. JS `#private` fields are the closest match, but Swift has five levels (`private`, `fileprivate`, `internal`, `package`, `public`/`open`), all checked at compile time.

compass.q: JS `#field` is enforced at runtime. TS `private` is compile-time only (erasable). Which does Swift's `private` resemble?

Can an extension in the same file see a `private` member? One in another file?
